correctness.rationale: For every connected simple finite unit-edge graph, the primal ball is the convex hull of oriented edges, so operator norm is evaluated on these edges and extreme dual heights. Any extreme dual height has connected tight-edge subgraph and therefore integer values, leaving only edge slopes -1,0,1. Unit slopes directly yield a numerical-radius pair. On zero slopes, all reweighted edges have length at least 1/2 and the selected edge length 1, hence its reweighted shortest distance is exactly 1 by simplicity. The distance potential plus/minus half the height gives two original-metric norming dual functionals whose difference is the height, proving ||T||<=2v(T). An explicit 2x2 real operator on the triangle has norm 1 and radius 1/2. Exact-rational verification for 48 finite graphs and the sharpness operator corroborates but does not replace the general proof. Boundaries: finite, connected, simple, unweighted, real.

value.rationale: Sharp dimension-free numerical radius equivalence for every operator on the entire, unbounded class of finite unweighted graph transportation spaces is a natural Banach-space invariant, with an exact global lower endpoint 1/2 realized already in a triangle. A constructive dual-face decomposition explains the mechanism. Unlike single finite examples or an upper-endpoint characterization, the inequality governs all nonbipartite graphs without requiring individual numerical-index calculations. Weighted graphs and infinite metric spaces remain open here.
